environment.description: Same application deployed on RHEL 9 host with a custom SELinux type enforcement policy (fileviewer_t). The policy module uses a narrow file context specification: only paths matching /var/app/data(/.*)? are labeled fileviewer_data_t, and the process domain fileviewer_t has read permission exclusively on type fileviewer_data_t and self-pipe types. The policy includes 'dontaudit fileviewer_t shadow_t:file { read open getattr };' and 'dontaudit fileviewer_t proc_t:file { read open };' which silently denies without logging. MLS sensitivity level s0 is enforced. The boolean httpd_can_network_connect is off. Policy compiled with semodule and enforcing mode confirmed via getenforce. Note: the dontaudit rules mean the application's try/catch blocks catch EACCES silently, so the background worker's fd opens to /etc/shadow and /proc/self/environ always fail - meaning recycled fds can only point to other fileviewer_data_t labeled files.

config.selinux_policy: custom module fileviewer version 1.0; type fileviewer_t; type fileviewer_data_t; allow fileviewer_t fileviewer_data_t:file { read open getattr }; allow fileviewer_t self:fifo_file { read write }; dontaudit fileviewer_t shadow_t:file { read open getattr }; dontaudit fileviewer_t proc_t:file { read open };
